svg.title: Winning Markup Bands
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-winning-markup-bands; chapter number: 4; title: Winning Markup Bands; subtitle: Where first wins and nine-figure bids were actually priced; caption: Dr. Wes Fisher compresses execution into five days, listing 15-20 opportunities and getting a quote within 48 hours. Derek James says bids 10-20 are in the money.; assumptions note: Each bucket is one practitioner's reported band, not a market survey. Kizzy Parks warns the hard part is funding, as with a $155,000 outlay for $10,000 in profit, and that upfront-cash, weird or overseas bids can sit outside the 7-25% band.; note: Sources - Kizzy Parks (etvo2gL7_Cs, AHQVro9N9HM, RrDUfb8vNms, WR8VA1o3VMU), with David Packouz and James Walk as reported by Parks.; chart type: stacked_comparison; total range: 7% to 25% markup, the contracting officer's middle band; buckets: label: Contracting Officer Middle Band; low: 7; high: 25; notes: A contracting officer told Kizzy Parks newcomers bid either too low or too high.; label: Gravel Sweet Spot; low: 10; high: 13; notes: The same contracting officer's band for gravel bids.; label: Packouz Munitions Margin; low: 10; high: 20; notes: Bid just under $300M and came in $52M under the next bidder, while majors bid around $500M.; label: James Walk VA Parts; low: 15; high: 15; notes: About $42K of VA Dallas cooling-tower parts, won under LPTA without being the lowest bidder.
